item.title: How Purges Are Affecting Chinese Military Readiness and Taiwan Contingencies
item.description: Since 2022, Chinese General Secretary Xi Jinping has purged at least 100 senior military officials, according to a February report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies, with more cases occurring since then. The rate of dismissals and disappearances has increased substantially in the last two years. Recent examples include Gen. Zhang Youxia, Gen. Liu Zhenli, and Zhong Shaojun, formerly the head of the General Office of the Central Military Commission. item.title: The Promise of Biomanufacturing at the Edge
item.description: As the old adage goes, “Amateurs talk strategy. Professionals talk logistics.” Military operations are utterly dependent on complex supply chains to move food, fuel, and other essential products across long distances and through contested environments to reach the warfighter. These vital supply lines are fragile at every stage: production concentrated in a single facility can be disrupted, key inputs may come from unreliable — or adversarial — foreign suppliers, and the ports, airfields, and roads that deliver goods the final mile are often the most vulnerable.The threat of this fragility eroding a modern force’s capabilities is very real. item.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
item.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. item.title: Oil Prices Head for Second Weekly Loss Despite Fresh Middle East Attacks
item.description: Crude oil prices were on course to book their second week of losses today, after two consecutive days of gains on news from the Middle East. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $95.87 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $88.49 per barrel. These price levels are a sharp decline from the peaks hit in mid-October, but are still significantly higher than what Brent crude and WTI traded at in February, before the war started. Signals about that war remain mixed. There appears to be only a moderate risk of serious escalation, but…

item.title: Oil Prices Squeezed Between Peace Hopes and Iran Escalation Risk
item.description: Oil prices have crashed about 20% from the late-October peak of $118 per barrel, weighed down by hopes of sustainable de-escalation in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war. For months, traders and hedge funds have often bet on a resolution of the conflicts, only to reactivate buying when talks fall apart. As U.S.-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia are underway, there are no signs of a breakthrough in either the conflict in Europe or the U.S.-Iran standoff, despite messaging via Qatar.
